The petitioner is an accused in connection with Narla P.S. Case No.50 of 2024 corresponding to C.T.
Case No.108 of 2024 for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC pending in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., M. Rampur.
The petitioner had approached the learned Additional Sessions Judge- cum-Special Judge (Vigilance), Bhawanipatna in BLAPL No.65/2 of 2024 praying for grant of bail.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.

The prosecution case is that, the informant had love relationship with the present petitioner.
They had kept physical relationship with the understanding of getting married.
It is alleged that on 26.02.2024, while the informant was in her uncle's house, the petitioner forcibly committed sexual assult on her.

Hence, the F.I.R.
4.

She, inter alia, stated that the petitioner had kept sexual relationship with her with promise to marry her.
5. I have perused the medical evidence of the victim from which it reveals that there is no recent sign or symptom of any sexual intercourse.
6. Regard being had to the fact that the petitioner has been in custody since 02.03.2024 and the nature of accusation, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

In the event the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.

opennyai_summary.decision:
7. Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper, subject to the following additional conditions:
(1) The petitioner shall appear before the Court below, without fail, on every date of hearing;
(2) He shall not influence any of the witnesses related to this case in any manner whatsoever and (3) The petitioner shall not commit any offence while on bail.
In the event the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
